text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today, extending a four-day rally that's recovered most of last week's losses. The bounce reflects a modest rebound in oil prices (US crude at $89.62/barrel) and continued strength in refined products—heating oil prices are up 59% from last year, which boosts margins for oil companies' refining operations. The stock has climbed $6 in the past four trading days after hitting a low of $134.47 on November 9th.

The recovery comes despite underlying headwinds: Russian crude production has rebounded to 8.73 million barrels per day following a Trump-era diesel deal, pushing global oil supplies back into surplus. That surplus pressure is a reminder of why the stock fell 7.6% over the past two weeks—when supply rises and demand softens, it typically weighs on both crude prices and the companies that produce it.
